chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Uzafir! You are dealing (co-operating) with Abu Ayoub and Al-Rabie, so what would your situation be when you are Called with among the supporters of the unjust ones?'

He (the narrator) said, 'My father was dumbfounded. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him when he saw what had hit him: 'Yes, Uzafir! But rather, I have scared you with what Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has Scared me with'.
Muhammad (the narrator) said, 'My father went forth and he did not cease to be gloomy, distressed, until he died'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of cooperating with unjust rulers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns Muhammad ibn Uzafir about the spiritual peril of serving unjust rulers, using the metaphor of being called among their 'supporters' on the Day of Judgment. The father's subsequent death while still in a state of gloom and distress illustrates the profound impact of this warning on his heart. This narrative highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *al-ghuraba* (the strangers) and the moral weight of administrative cooperation with tyranny, a theme central to the concept of *al-wala' wa al-barra'*.

en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn ‘Adha’fir from his father who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O ‘Adha’fir, you cooperate with abu Ayyub and al-Rabi‘, how will your condition be when you will be called along with the helpers of unjust ones?

He (the narrator) has said that my father became extremely depressed and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, upon seeing the condition of my father said, ‘O ‘Adha’fir, I alarmed you the way Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has alarmed me.’
Muhammad has said, ‘My father came home and continued to remain depressed until he died.’”
